ASML peer / Advantest via ADR.role: Advantest is a dominant supplier of automated test equipment (ATE) for logic and memory chips, benefiting from AI-driven demand for testing complex GPUs/HBM, but its revenue is tied to cyclical semiconductor capex and WFE spending.

Synopsys.role: Synopsys dominates the EDA duopoly providing indispensable chip design software and IP; recurring, mission-critical demand and high switching costs make it durable AI-infra picks-and-shovels with modest but secular growth.

Intel.role: Integrated x86 chipmaker attempting a costly foundry/IDM 2.0 transformation; sits mid-quality with cyclical earnings, eroded share vs TSMC/AMD/Nvidia, and heavy execution risk that keeps beta and permanence elevated.

GlobalFoundries.role: GlobalFoundries is a specialty foundry focused on mature/differentiated nodes for auto, IoT, RF and industrial rather than leading-edge AI logic, so it captures secondary AI-adjacent demand while remaining cyclical, capex-sensitive, and lacking leading-edge moat versus TSMC.

onsemi.role: onsemi supplies power management and silicon-carbide devices for autos, industrial and increasingly AI data-center power delivery; it sits in AI-infra but with cyclical exposure since most revenue is auto/industrial with only nascent AI-power contribution amid flat top-line growth.

Analog Devices.role: ADI is a leading high-performance analog and mixed-signal chipmaker serving industrial, automotive, communications, and data-center markets; broad diversification and sticky designs give durability, but its end demand is cyclical and only partly AI-levered, placing it in AI-infra with moderate perma

NXP Semiconductors.role: NXP supplies automotive and industrial microcontrollers, processors, and connectivity chips with strong exposure to vehicle electrification and edge compute; it sits in AI-infra with moderate growth and cyclicality tied to auto/industrial end-markets.

Skyworks Solutions.role: Skyworks supplies RF front-end modules dominated by mobile handset (heavy Apple concentration) demand; it sits as a mature, cyclical semiconductor name with limited direct AI exposure and flat-to-declining revenue amid smartphone softness.

Qorvo.role: Qorvo supplies RF front-end modules and filters heavily levered to smartphone cycles (notably Apple/Android handsets); its cyclical mobile concentration and flat-to-declining revenue place it as a mid-quality, capex-sensitive semi name with limited direct AI exposure.

Entegris.role: Supplier of high-purity materials, filtration, and specialty chemicals consumed in chip fabrication; recurring consumables tied to wafer volumes give it durability, but exposure to fab utilization and capex cycles keeps it moderately cyclical.

MKS Instruments.role: MKS supplies critical subsystems (vacuum, RF power, lasers, motion, optics) and materials to semiconductor equipment makers and fabs; it benefits from AI-driven fab investment but remains cyclical, capex-dependent, and carries meaningful leverage post-Atotech, tempering earnings durability.

Onto Innovation.role: Onto supplies metrology and inspection equipment for advanced packaging and logic/memory fabs, benefiting from AI-driven packaging complexity but exposed to cyclical semi-cap spending and competition from larger metrology peers.

FormFactor.role: FormFactor makes probe cards and test systems used in semiconductor manufacturing; it holds a leading share in advanced probe cards benefiting from HBM/AI chip test intensity, but its revenue is tied to cyclical wafer-test capex, keeping earnings durability moderate.

Photronics.role: Photronics makes photomasks (reticles) essential to chip fabrication, a critical but mature niche input; flat TTM revenue growth and cyclical foundry/IC demand cap upside, placing it as a moderate-moat supplier tied to semiconductor capex cycles.

Cohu.role: Cohu supplies test handlers, contactors and interface products for semiconductor back-end test; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical, capex-driven supplier with moderate share and durability tied to the semi equipment cycle rather than secular AI demand.

indie Semiconductor.role: Fabless designer of automotive semiconductors and ADAS/edge-AI SoCs for vision, radar and connectivity; sits in disruptive due to sub-scale revenue, persistent losses, cyclical auto exposure, and dependence on design-win ramps despite decelerating single-digit YoY growth.

Allegro MicroSystems.role: Allegro designs magnetic sensor and power ICs concentrated in automotive (especially EV/ADAS) and industrial markets; solid niche leadership but cyclical auto/industrial exposure and modest single-digit growth keep it a mid-quality cyclical rather than an AI secular play.

Power Integrations.role: Fabless leader in high-voltage power conversion ICs serving consumer, industrial, and increasingly data-center power delivery; flat recent growth and cyclical end-markets keep it a modest-growth, mid-quality AI-adjacent play rather than a core AI compute name.

Vishay Intertechnology.role: Broad-line supplier of discrete semiconductors and passive components serving industrial, automotive, and comms end-markets; cyclical commodity-like exposure with modest AI-datacenter power tailwind but fragmented competition and thin growth make it a lower-conviction cyclical rather than a secular

Diodes Incorporated.role: Diodes makes commodity analog and discrete components for consumer, industrial, and automotive end-markets; broad but low-differentiation exposure with modest AI relevance makes it a cyclical, fragmented-moat player rather than a core AI-infrastructure beneficiary.

Semtech.role: Analog/mixed-signal semiconductor maker with LoRa IoT connectivity and data-center signal integrity products; mid-cap cyclical with modest growth and moderate moat, hence mid-tier quality and elevated beta.

MaxLinear peer Cirrus.role: Cirrus is a mixed-signal semiconductor maker heavily reliant on smartphone audio and haptics with major customer concentration (Apple), making earnings cyclical and consumer-demand-sensitive rather than AI-secular; modest growth and single-customer risk keep quality and permanence mid-range.

Impinj.role: Impinj is the leading provider of RAIN RFID chips and readers for retail/supply-chain item tracking; strong endpoint IC share gives it a moat, but its revenue is inventory-cyclical and tied to retail capex, keeping it a volatile mid-cap rather than an AI-secular name.

Airgain.role: Small-cap designer of antenna and wireless connectivity systems for IoT, automotive, and enterprise; flat revenue, thin margins, and a fragmented competitive market make it a speculative micro-cap with limited moat.

Pegasystems.role: Enterprise BPM/CRM platform pivoting to AI-driven workflow automation with a transition to recurring cloud/subscription revenue; flat-to-slightly-negative TTM revenue and a crowded competitive field cap upside, but sticky enterprise contracts and improving margins support moderate durability.

Twilio.role: Twilio provides programmable cloud communications (CPaaS) APIs increasingly layered with AI-driven customer engagement; solid recurring revenue but modest single-digit growth, competitive fragmentation, and usage-based cyclicality place it as a mid-quality AI-platform name.

Dropbox.role: Mature cloud file storage/collaboration vendor with flat revenue; AI (Dash) is an unproven adjacency, so it sits as a defensive low-growth name rather than a genuine AI beneficiary.

Box.role: Box is a mature enterprise content-management SaaS layering AI features (Box AI) onto its file storage platform; low single-digit growth, decent recurring revenue and modest valuation place it as a defensive tech name with only a speculative AI upside kicker.

Amdocs.role: Amdocs provides mission-critical billing, monetization, and OSS software to telecom carriers with long recurring contracts; it sits as a defensive, low-growth incumbent where AI is an incremental efficiency layer rather than a transformative growth driver.

Verint Systems.role: Verint sells AI-powered customer engagement and workforce optimization software with a recurring SaaS base, but flat revenue, modest scale, and competitive pressure from larger CX platforms cap its AI upside and keep it in the mature/defensive bucket.

NICE Ltd.role: NICE is a leading cloud contact-center and customer-engagement software vendor (CXone) embedding generative AI agents; recurring SaaS revenue supports durability but decelerating growth and AI-disruption risk to seat-based models temper its multiple.

Fortinet.role: Fortinet is a profitable network-security vendor with strong firewall hardware and expanding SASE/AI software; recurring subscriptions and healthy margins make it durable, though maturing growth and firewall refresh cyclicality temper upside.

Okta.role: Okta provides cloud identity and access management with recurring subscription revenue; decelerating growth (~2.6% YoY) and competition from Microsoft cap upside, but sticky enterprise identity spend and non-discretionary security budgets support durability, placing it in defensive despite modest AI

Tenable Holdings.role: Cybersecurity vendor specializing in vulnerability and exposure management with an AI-security tilt; recurring subscription revenue and non-discretionary security spend give durability, but slow ~2% growth and a fragmented, competitive market cap its upside and AI leverage.

Qualys.role: Qualys sells recurring cloud-based vulnerability management and compliance SaaS; its highly profitable subscription model and sticky enterprise base make it defensive, but ~3% growth reflects intense competition in a crowded security market with limited AI differentiation.

Varonis Systems.role: Data-security software vendor pivoting to SaaS and AI-data-governance; recurring subscription revenue and non-discretionary security spend make demand relatively resilient, but modest ~5% reported growth and a crowded cybersecurity market limit its moat and cap upside.

Bentley Systems.role: Provides engineering and infrastructure design software (BIM/digital twins) with a largely recurring subscription base; AI is an incremental feature layer rather than a core growth driver, so it sits as a durable, moderately-growing defensive name with modest AI upside.

PTC.role: PTC provides PLM, CAD, and IoT software for manufacturers with a largely subscription/ARR base; industrial AI is an incremental overlay rather than a core driver, so it sits as a durable but slow-growth defensive software name.

Salesforce.role: Dominant SaaS CRM vendor layering agentic AI (Agentforce) onto a large recurring-revenue base; growth is modest but earnings are durable and demand is largely non-discretionary, placing it as a quality AI-platform name rather than a hyper-growth story.

Digital Realty Trust.role: Global data center REIT leasing colocation and interconnection capacity to hyperscalers and enterprises; sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels landlord with recurring lease income, but growth is modest and high P/E reflects REIT accounting (FFO) rather than pure AI hyper-growth.

Equinix.role: Equinix operates a global network of colocation data centers and interconnection hubs (REIT structure) with recurring lease/interconnect revenue; it benefits indirectly from AI-driven demand but grows steadily rather than explosively, warranting a durable, moderate-risk profile.

Iron Mountain.role: Records-management REIT expanding into data center colocation; the AI-relevant data center segment is a small but growing slice of a highly recurring, contract-anchored revenue base, giving it defensive earnings but limited scale versus hyperscale-focused peers.

GE Vernova.role: GE Vernova supplies gas turbines, grid equipment, and electrification hardware that underpin datacenter power demand; it sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels beneficiary of AI-driven electricity load, but with cyclical utility/project exposure and modest single-digit topline growth.

Eaton.role: Diversified electrical equipment maker supplying power distribution, switchgear and backup systems to data centers; a credible AI-infrastructure beneficiary but revenue is broad-based and partly cyclical, so only a portion is AI-levered.

Schneider peer Hubbell.role: Hubbell makes utility and electrical grid components benefiting from grid modernization and datacenter power buildout; it sits in defensive with moderate growth given its diversified, non-speculative but partly cyclical infrastructure exposure.

Emerson Electric.role: Diversified industrial automation leader whose process control and software (Aspen, discrete/hybrid automation) benefit from factory digitalization and data-center power/cooling demand, but core revenue remains cyclical and capex-linked, only partially AI-driven.

Johnson Controls.role: Diversified building-systems and HVAC provider whose thermal management and liquid-cooling portfolio serves data centers; only a slice of its ~$25bn revenue is AI-relevant, so it sits as a moderate-beta AI-infra play with cyclical capex exposure.

Generac Holdings.role: Leading maker of residential/commercial backup generators and energy storage; a cyclical, weather- and housing-sensitive industrial with a strong home-standby franchise but only a tangential AI/data-center power angle, hence defensive-cyclical positioning.

Oklo.role: Pre-revenue developer of small modular fast reactors targeting data-center and AI power demand; speculative because commercial deployment is years away with no NRC-licensed operating plant or revenue yet.

Centrus Energy.role: Centrus enriches uranium and is the only U.S.-owned licensed HALEU producer, positioning it as a strategic nuclear fuel supplier; it sits in disruptive due to policy-driven upside on advanced reactors but faces cyclical demand, execution risk, and heavy government dependence.

MasTec.role: Diversified infrastructure/EPC contractor with a communications and power-delivery segment increasingly tied to data center and grid build-outs; cyclical project-based revenue with modest AI exposure and a fragmented, competitive market limits pricing power and durability.

ARKK (ARK Innovation).role: disruptive-innovation basket LED BY TESLA (~10%), then AMD, CRISPR, Tempus AI, Robinhood. High beta, rich multiples, Tesla-driven idiosyncratic swings — NOT a semis basket.

QQQ (Nasdaq-100).role: Nasdaq-100 mega-cap tech; quality, but rich and tech-tilted.

VOO (S&P 500).role: broad US large-cap; the market itself — durable, diversified.

SCHD (Dividend).role: quality-dividend value basket; low beta, cheap, durable earnings.

DTCR (Data Ctr Infra).role: data-center REITs & digital infra (Equinix, Digital Realty, American Tower); physical, contracted, durable — low beta.

GRID (Smart Grid).role: grid/power equipment for the AI electricity demand (Eaton, Quanta, GE Vernova); inelastic infra spend.

NUKE (Nuclear/Uranium).role: nuclear/uranium for data-center baseload (Constellation, Vistra, Cameco, BWX); high-growth but cyclical/volatile.

VGT (Info Tech).role: broad US information-technology sector; mega-cap heavy, durable.

IGV (Software).role: application & infrastructure software basket; higher multiple, subscription-durable.
